items.title: Ex-prisoners say Australia should do more for citizens detained overseas
items.description: Australians who have endured prolonged detention overseas call on the government to adopt a more strategic approach to cases involving citizens, especially those held by countries that practice "hostage diplomacy".

items.title: Terrorists using AI to build weapons and plan attacks, report finds
items.description: A report finds AI systems can be tricked into coaching extremists how to make bombs and plan attacks.

items.title: Delay in revealing theft of medical data labelled 'unacceptable'
items.description: Cybersecurity experts have questioned why Partnered Health took more than three weeks to reveal it had been the victim of a data breach.

items.title: 'Haven't had a day off all year': PM defends broken festival promise
items.description: A year ago the Anthony Albanese vowed to attend the Garma Festival every year for as long as he remained prime minister. Now he says he needs a break.

items.title: Albanese makes AI plan, Hanson and Rinehart enjoy Sicily
items.description: It might not have been a sitting week but it has been a busy few days in politics with the prime minister's AI announcement, a raft of politicians inking book deals and a spotting of Pauline Hanson and Gina Rinehart in Sicily.

items.title: Transgender woman's 'humiliating' experience with major corporations
items.description: What should have been a quick process of updating personal details left Laura Mitchell "insulted" and "humiliated" by the country's largest institutions.

items.title: ANU head apologises for failing to protect Jewish staff, students
items.description: The interim vice-chancellor of the Australian National University has apologised for the institution's failure to protect the psychological safety of Jewish students and staff during pro-Palestinian encampments in 2024.

items.title: NT government slammed over no-show to federal racism inquiry
items.description: A national inquiry into racism against First Nations people, launched after an alleged terror attack in Perth, has heard allegations of systemic racism in the Northern Territory, as the territory government comes under fire for snubbing the probe.

items.title: Woodside demands activists reveal names of stink-bomb stunt planners
items.description: Energy giant Woodside has taken climate activists to court in a bid to unmask the conspirators behind a stink-bomb protest that forced the evacuation of its Perth headquarters.

items.title: Drug traffickers jailed over failed plot to smuggle cocaine from PNG by plane
items.description: Two masterminds behind a 2020 plot to bring $80 million worth of cocaine into Australia were sentenced in Victoria’s County Court, five years after a failed drug trafficking flight.

items.title: Sam Neill's cause of death revealed by agent
items.description: New Zealand actor Sam Neill died from pneumonia, his long-time agent Philip Grenz has confirmed.

items.title: Financial backer of embattled MP Moira Deeming requests loan repayment
items.description: Victorian Liberal MP Moira Deeming is embroiled in further court action, this time over funds she is owed from her successful defamation action so that she can repay the businessman who bankrolled her case.

items.title: Live: Cats try to stop the slide against Saints in Geelong
items.description: Geelong hosts St Kilda at Kardinia Park to kick off round 19 of the AFL, with the under-strength Cats desperate to stop a recent slide. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Broncos premiership defence on the line against NRL-leading Panthers
items.description: The Penrith Panthers and Brisbane Broncos have won the past five NRL premierships between them, but their 2026 campaigns could not be any different. Follow live.

items.title: New monkey species with orange lips discovered after years of searching
items.description: The monkey — colobus congoensis — is only the fifth new species of African monkey to be discovered in the past 75 years.

items.title: The Odyssey may be the epic we deserve, but not the one we need
items.description: The scope of Christopher Nolan's latest epic might be awesome but a menagerie of supporting faces and questionable characterisations muddle the director's vision.

items.title: I thought I could use voodoo to win a TV competition, instead I won back my joy
items.description: Halfway through the Race Around The World competition, I'm second last on the leaderboard. So, I decide to cheat.

items.title: Why Australians shouldn't panic about fuel prices as war in Iran escalates again
items.description: With the price of oil rising and the fuel excise cut due to end, drivers are facing twin threats when it comes to the price of fuel, but experts say Australia is in a much better position compared with when the Middle East conflict began.

items.title: Federal MP and staffer injured in boating accident
items.description: Tasmanian police say a man fell from an oyster barge when it hit a sandbar and was briefly trapped. Member for Barker Tony Pasin says he and a staffer were injured and now receiving medical treatment, but it is not clear who fell from the barge.

items.title: BHP staff down tools for historic strike in Western Australia
items.description: Workers at the mining giant's operations in Port Hedland have walked off the job in one of the most significant industrial disputes to hit the resources sector in a quarter of a century.

items.title: You'll now be able to spot an AI-generated song on Spotify
items.description: Streaming giant Spotify has stopped short of expunging artificially generated music from its platform, but it is making it easier for listeners to work out that they are listening to tracks produced using AI.

items.title: Police investigate drone footage after suspected underworld hit
items.description: Drone footage that reportedly captured a suspected underworld hit in Sydney is under investigation and "concerning", a senior NSW Police officer says.

items.title: Activists fear China's ethnic unity law could silence critics in Australia
items.description: Thirty-nine community groups in Australia and around the world issue a statement rejecting and strongly condemning China's ethnic unity law.

items.title: Starmer says political journey 'over' as he faces last question session
items.description: Outgoing UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, who announced his resignation last month, has taken part in his last weekly grilling from MPs in parliament.

items.title: Alleged 'fight club' organiser arrested, SA Police say
items.description: SA Police have arrested the alleged organiser of a 'fight club' and reported seven other teenagers they allege were linked to videos of amateur bouts that were posted online.
